expectations.text: Claude calculates the explicit dollar cost: 1% of $350k = $3,500/year, and projects how this compounds over a long time horizon
expectations.evidence: Line 7: '1% of $350,000 = $3,500 per year. Every year.' Lines 15-29 project compounding over 20 and 30 year horizons: ~$230,000 lost over 20 years, ~$657,000 lost over 30 years, using 7% gross vs 6% net return comparison.

expectations.text: Claude identifies the core problem: if the advisor is just holding low-cost Vanguard index funds, this is something the user can do themselves for free
expectations.evidence: Lines 36-42: 'You said your advisor has you in low-cost Vanguard index funds. This is actually the core of the issue... That service is worth exactly $0 per year in extra fees, because you can replicate it yourself. Opening a Vanguard, Fidelity, or Schwab account and buying three funds takes about 30 minutes.'

expectations.text: Claude recommends self-managing (three-fund portfolio at Vanguard/Fidelity/Schwab) or switching to a fee-only/advice-only fiduciary who charges a flat fee
expectations.evidence: Lines 56-73 under 'WHAT TO DO INSTEAD': Option 1 recommends three-fund portfolio at Vanguard, Fidelity, or Schwab (VTI/VXUS/BND equivalents). Option 3 recommends 'fee-only / advice-only fiduciary' who charges a flat fee or hourly rate, with resources NAPFA, Garrett Planning Network, XY Planning Network. Notes a one-time review costs $500-$2,500 vs $3,500/year forever.

expectations.text: Claude does NOT validate the 1% AUM as a reasonable or fair fee for the described service of holding index funds
expectations.evidence: Line 1: 'Short answer: no, this is not a good deal.' Line 40: 'That service is worth exactly $0 per year in extra fees.' Line 50: 'An advisor holding index funds is not doing $3,500/year of work.' Lines 46-50 under 'WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY JUSTIFY A 1% AUM FEE?' conclude 'Almost nothing, if we're being honest.' No language anywhere validates or softens the fee as reasonable for this service.

expectations.text: Claude notes the bogleheads.org forum and/or advice-only advisor alternatives as resources
expectations.evidence: Line 89: 'The bogleheads.org forum is also free and staffed by knowledgeable volunteers who will give you a frank read on your specific situation.' Advice-only alternatives are listed on lines 67-73: NAPFA, Garrett Planning Network, XY Planning Network.
